name: unnamed periodic counter message
summary: A 40-byte message whose body is identical across its four captured instances except the last byte, which counts 01, 02, 03, 04. It is a keepalive, not an event, and it shares its tail envelope with LevelInfoChangedMsg.
purpose: Keep the session alive on a timer. The incrementing final byte is a sequence number, which is what a keepalive needs and what an event does not.

created_when: periodically while the client is in or entering the world
lifecycle.if_absent: unknown; a keepalive that stops is the usual cause of a silent disconnect, which is consistent with the lab's observed 10 s drop after silence

fields.name: typed_header
fields.note: Measured 00 01 a6 62: the typed envelope plus the prefix varint a6 62 = 0x18a6.

fields.name: unresolved_id_at_0x04
fields.note: Measured f8 cb ed 57 c6 8b 18 f4 bf 85 31 4b bc 4a 95 1a, identical in all four instances. As a GUID with the first three fields little-endian it is 57EDCBF8-8BC6-F418-BF85-314BBC4A951A. It is NOT the player's actor id (1a954abc4b3185bfbe37c3d8592618e0), so it names something else.

fields.name: flags_at_0x14
fields.note: Measured 01 01 00 00, the same four bytes that open the level-info tail. Shared envelope, meaning unknown.

fields.name: session_nonce
fields.note: Measured 9c fa 58 61 78 14 69 f2, the SAME value that LevelInfoChangedMsg carries at 0x54. Two different message types sharing a value is the strongest kind of field evidence in this inventory, and the value differs per session rather than per record, which is why it is called a session nonce.

fields.name: unresolved_tag_at_0x20
fields.note: Measured 65 03 00 00 00 00, also present at the same place in the level-info tail. 65 03 00 00 is 869 as a little-endian u32, which reads like a version or protocol tag; unproven.

fields.name: sequence_counter
fields.note: The last byte of the record. Measured 01 at seq 0x0b, 02 at seq 0x38, 03 at seq 0x53, 04 at seq 0x68: it increments once per message, in capture order. The byte before it is 0x02 in all four instances.

evidence.ref: records 0xb_T0x18a6_R.bin, 0x38_T0x18a6_R.bin, 0x53_T0x18a6_R.bin and 0x68_T0x18a6_R.bin, 40 bytes each, at seq 0x0b, 0x38, 0x53 and 0x68. Their bodies are byte-identical except the final byte, which is 01, 02, 03, 04 in that order

the 8-byte value 9c fa 58 61 78 14 69 f2 sits at offset 0x18 here and at 0x54 in the level-info record 0x10_T0x663_R.bin, after the same four flag bytes 01 01 00 00 and before the same six bytes 65 03 00 00 00 00

research/derived/wire-type-names.json reports no name for slot 6310, and a direct dump of that GUID's surroundings shows only pointer qwords before it, so the name is not recoverable from .rdata adjacency and this concept stays unnamed on purpose
